asDecan.p: Every sign is cut into three slices of ten degrees, called decans, and each slice gets a planet and a numbered card. Your Sun is somewhere between 20 and 29 degrees of Libra, the last slice, and in the Chaldean order that stretch goes to Jupiter. Jupiter has no dignity in Libra, good or bad. It's a visitor there, so it goes along with Venus, who rules the sign and wants things pleasant and fair, and then adds its own habit of making whatever it touches bigger and more generous. The two slices before yours are quite different. The Two belongs to the Moon and holds two options without picking either. The Three is Saturn's, and it's the heartbreak card. Yours comes straight after that, a knight lying flat in a chapel with his hands together, having a proper rest. Justice is your Sun card and covers the whole of Libra. The Four is just your ten degrees, right at the end of the sign where it's already leaning toward Scorpio, and that's partly why people with the Sun here keep a good deal to themselves.

You're the one people ring after the argument, and you're good at it. Your sister and your mum fall out over who's hosting Christmas, and somehow it's you on the phone to each of them in turn, making it sound a bit less final than it did an hour ago. After a meeting that went badly, you send the friendly email that gets everybody talking again. You also need a surprising amount of quiet for someone so sociable. A Saturday with nothing in the diary is how you get back to level after a week of being nice to everyone, and you guard it fiercely, whatever you tell people. When a text comes in that's a bit sharp, you leave it overnight before you answer. By morning you've found the generous way to read it, and to be honest you're usually right.

You're good at letting other people off the hook for being tired. Plenty of people are kind, but Jupiter in this slice makes you generous with time and slack, which is rarer. A friend is running on fumes, caring for a parent and working full time, and you say go home, I'll sort the school pickup, and you mean it so plainly that they actually go. At work you notice the colleague who hasn't taken leave in eighteen months and quietly mention it to the right person. There's no speech about self-care. You rest yourself, without apologising for it, and after a while the people around you start doing the same. I see this a lot with late Libra Suns. Six months after one of them joins a team, people have started eating lunch away from their desks.

Rest is a very respectable reason to put something off, and you know how to use it. 'I just need a quiet weekend first' sounds healthy, so nobody argues, and the talk with your partner about money gets moved to after the weekend, then after the holidays, and it's still waiting when autumn comes round again. Jupiter is an optimist, and with Venus setting the tone it leans toward hoping things will settle by themselves if nobody pushes. Sometimes they do, and sometimes the friend who keeps cancelling on you just never hears that it bothers you, so they keep doing it. There's a spending side as well, because Jupiter and Venus both like comfort and Jupiter likes a lot of it. The good sheets, the long lunch, the weekend away to get over a week that honestly wasn't that bad. When the same conversation has been put off for three weekends running, have it on the fourth, tired or not.

When something goes badly wrong, a redundancy, a friendship ending, a family row you couldn't smooth over, you go polite first. For the first few days you're gracious to everyone and fine, thanks, really. About a week later you vanish. Early nights, phone face down, the curtains half shut on a Sunday afternoon. That's the Four of Swords doing its job, and it's genuinely how you recover, but the people close to you often don't see it coming, because on the surface you were coping beautifully. Your partner ends up guessing what's wrong, and guessing wrong, and a friend who rang twice decides you're annoyed with them. It helps a lot to tell one person that you're going quiet and roughly for how long. Then sleep, plain food, a walk somewhere with trees, and someone you trust who comes round and doesn't need you to be pleasant while they're there.

You're quick to forgive, and in this slice it's big forgiveness, Jupiter-sized. A partner says something cruel in a fight and by the next morning you've put it down, which is lovely, except that sometimes you've put it down before they've actually said sorry. Over a few years that teaches someone they don't need to. The Scorpio edge of your degrees shows up here as well. You look easygoing and you want more depth than you let on, and the relationships that last tend to be with people who can sit through a long, honest conversation without getting defensive. You also need someone who doesn't take your quiet weekends personally. Tell them early, before they've had the chance to worry, that when you disappear into the couch for a day it isn't about them.

Justice is your Sun card, and in this slice it gets a particular job. The two earlier Libra decans do the weighing up. You're better at what comes after the verdict, when people still have to work together on Monday. The ward manager on nights after a hard shift, whoever runs front of house when the kitchen's just had a blow-up, a school counsellor, a team leader after a restructure, a physio, someone who runs a good small hotel. People arrive rattled and leave steadier, and that's the work you're built for. Jupiter gives you a long view, so one bad quarter doesn't frighten you much. The catch is pace. You work well in bursts and then need real recovery, and a job with no slack in it wears you down faster than it would most people. Take your full annual leave, all of it, and book it before you're desperate for it.

At twenty this decan usually shows up as saying yes to everything and everyone, being the peacemaker in every share house and friendship group, and then crashing flat for a week and not really knowing why. The rest happens, but only when the body forces it. By the mid-thirties most people with a Sun here have learnt to schedule the quiet on purpose, and to say no a bit earlier. Fewer people ring them at eleven at night, and most of them are fine with that. The fifties often bring the role of the calm older friend, the one people visit when their own lives have got too loud. The thing to watch then is withdrawing a bit too comfortably, letting the quiet get so pleasant that you stop turning up to things you'd actually enjoy.

Pick one evening a week and put it in your calendar as unavailable, with no reason given. That evening, from dinner until bed, the phone stays switched off in a drawer. Don't fill the time with chores or catch-up emails. Lie on the floor, read, have a long bath, do nothing much. If someone asks you out that night, say you've already got plans, because you have. Keep it going for a month and see what happens to the other six evenings.
